dct_description_sm: The Canadian Permafrost Monitoring Network provides long-term field observations of permafrost thermal state and active layer thickness. This is a contribution to the Global Terrestrial Network for Permafrost (GTN-P) which was established in 1999 by the International Permafrost Association and is part of the World Meteorological Organization's Global Climate Observing System. See http://nsidc.org/data/ggd633.html for metadata for GTN-P. The Canadian network at present consists of over 150 monitoring sites, several of which have operated for 2 to 3 decades or longer. Since 2005 through various funding initiatives including the International Polar Year, approximately 80 new sites have been established to increase the coverage of the network. These data facilitate the characterization of regional baseline conditions and quantification of recent change in permafrost thermal state and active layer thickness. Data generated by the network meets the needs of scientists, permafrost and climate change modellers, engineers, landuse planners, regulators and policy/decision makers. Summary data are publicly disseminated through a number of means with summary data posted on the network web site. The data set contributes to a number of different programs/projects including the IPY projects Thermal State of Permafrost, TSP-Canada and Variability and Change in the Canadian Cryosphere.
